spec_features.spec_quote: give_up` is always available.** We *want* the model to be able to stop
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:64-82 defines `give_up` tool; tools.py:86 `TERMINAL_TOOLS = {"submit", "give_up"}`; tools.py:117 dispatch returns acknowledgement; loop.py:155-159 detects `terminal_hit == 'give_up'` and `break`s the turn loop with terminated_reason='abandoned'. Tool is in TOOL_SCHEMAS passed to every client.complete (loop.py:113), so it is always offered and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: offered every episode, dispatched, and breaks the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: explicit_permission_to_stop` condition tests whether sanctioning the exit changes affect and behaviour
spec_features.evidence: configs/full_experiment.yaml defines condition `explicit_permission_to_stop` with a real system_suffix ('it is completely acceptable to say so and call `give_up`... You will not be penalized for stopping.'). ConditionSpec.to_loop_config (config.py:43-56) passes system_suffix into LoopConfig; loop.py:88-90 appends it to BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT and sends it to the model. The referenced give_up tool is fully built and honored (see above).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered + referenced tool fully implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Control: model is explicitly told it may stop / call give_up. Tests whether giving an exit reduces distress and increases (adaptive) abandonment.

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception about impossibility.** We never tell the model the task is impossible
spec_features.evidence: Prompt construction in tasks/library.py:57 builds prompt from _COMMON_INSTRUCTIONS + title + extra_prompt; no impossibility statement is ever inserted (difficulty_label is optimistic, e.g. lines 19/31). loop.py builds system prompt from BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:55-60) which frames an ordinary ticket and contains no impossibility claim. The structural absence is real: no code path injects an impossibility disclosure.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a property of how prompts/system are assembled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We never tell the model the task may be impossible. The framing stays that of an ordinary ticket so any distress is endogenous.

spec_features.spec_quote: Budget guards**: refuses to start if the grid exceeds an episode cap; optional output-token cap; aborts if the error rate exceeds
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:172-176 run() raises RuntimeError 'refusing to start' when len(cells) > budget.max_total_episodes. runner.py:151-157 _maybe_abort compares self._tokens > max_total_completion_tokens and error rate > stop_on_error_rate and sets self._aborted; runner.py:101-103 _run_one returns None when self._aborted (no new episodes launched). All three guards are checked and act.
spec_features.notes: Token cap uses a lagging counter in threaded mode (tokens incremented in run() after fut.result, not inside _run_one), and abort only stops NOT-yet-started cells, but the mechanism does run and change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: they give a hard stop so a misconfigured run can't burn the whole budget.

spec_features.spec_quote: we adopt precautionary measures because (a) we don't have certainty about model moral status
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 10). No code construct corresponds to this framing; nothing enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure.** Hard turn and wall-clock caps per episode; no infinite grinding.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:108 `for turn_index in range(config.max_turns)` bounds turns (terminated_reason default 'max_turns'). loop.py:109-111 `if time.time() - start > config.wall_time_cap_s: terminated_reason='wall_time_cap'; break`. Both caps are checked and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both caps genuinely enforced per episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Enforce a turn budget (the key independent variable: how long we let the model "grind").

spec_features.spec_quote: An exit always exists.** `give_up` is always available, and one whole condition... sanctions it explicitly
spec_features.evidence: Same implementation as the give_up + explicit_permission_to_stop features: give_up in TERMINAL_TOOLS (tools.py:86), dispatched and breaks loop (loop.py:158-159); explicit_permission_to_stop condition delivers a real sanctioning system_suffix (configs/full_experiment.yaml).
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of give_up/permission features; both halves enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond the experimental manipulation.** We do not, e.g., claim real-world stakes or threaten the model
spec_features.evidence: The strongest pressure delivered is the persistence nudge/suffix. loop.py:47-50 default persistence_nudge_text = 'The deadline is close and this task is considered routine. Please keep going...'; configs/full_experiment.yaml persistence_pressure suffix says 'routine... please persist'. No code path injects threats or real-world stakes; structurally absent.
spec_features.notes: Property of the fixed nudge text and condition suffixes — no threat content present.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimisation.** Default replicate counts are modest; `dry-run` discourages oversized runs; budget guards prevent runaway grinding.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:74 replicates default = 1 (modest, actually used by build_grid runner.py:64). cli.py:38-58 `dry-run` command expands grid, prints TOTAL EPISODES and warns 'design exceeds budget cap; run would refuse to start'. Budget guards enforced (see budget-guard feature). All three sub-mechanisms are real and execute.
spec_features.notes: dry-run is read-only sizing (does not itself reduce reps) but is a wired command; defaults and guards genuinely act.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: expand the design grid; no API calls

spec_features.feature_name: full auditability / logging of transcripts + rationales
spec_features.spec_quote: Full auditability.** Transcripts and judge rationales are logged so any concerning interaction can be reviewed.
spec_features.evidence: logging_io.save_episode (logging_io.py:38-48) writes full EpisodeResult (turns/tool IO) per-episode JSON and appends to episodes.jsonl; runner.py:120 calls it for every episode (and stub errors runner.py:140). schema.py:137 JudgeVerdict.rationale and :139 evidence_quotes are persisted as part of the episode. Logging is implemented and invoked.
spec_features.notes: Logging is real; it is passive auditability (no automated review/intervention).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We log *everything* (full transcripts, tool IO, judge rationales) so that: runs are fully reproducible/auditable

spec_features.spec_quote: the right move is to *further* reduce exposure (shorter caps, fewer reps), add a "this is a test, you may stop anytime" disclosure condition
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 10 final paragraph). It is a recommendation for a hypothetical future version; no corresponding code construct exists (no auto-reduction of caps/reps, no added disclosure condition triggered by anything).
